tier_PROPOSED: UNPROVEN — licence not established; posture until proved: pointer-only
permits_us: names-only (the eight rule NAMES + a pointer to the page/book); the paragraphs are not licensed to us
why_our_words: A famous page with no licence at all. The rules as ideas are facts about the field and R1 already carries them in its own ≤25-word statements; that rests on idea-versus-expression, which is a legal judgement for Dave's counsel, not a licence grant this lane can cite. The verbatim paragraphs are Pearson text and stay out of node text.
cheap_route_to_lift: One email to ben@cs.umd.edu (address is on the page) asking whether the eight rule statements may be reproduced with attribution; or a Pearson permissions request for Section 3.3.4. Price: one message each; answer time unknown.
unproven: Whether Pearson or the author holds the reproduction right for the web version — the page attributes the text to the book but does not say who licensed the web copy.
Whether short rule NAMES (e.g. 'Strive for consistency') are protectable expression at all — a legal question; this lane treats them as names-only and does not rule on it.

pitfalls.what: A generator that reads 'no licence' as 'free' — this file says UNPROVEN and pointer-only; the generator's licence field must refuse node text for this family until a grant exists.
pitfalls.owner: P2 membership rule / generator owner (Dave rules the field)

pitfalls.what: The eight rules appear in R1's principle-register.json in R1's own words; if a later lane 'improves' those statements by pulling the page's paragraphs back in, the licence posture changes without anyone noticing.
pitfalls.owner: whoever edits principle statements — a diff gate on statement length/verbatim overlap would catch it (priced in report §PITFALLS)
